title: Words of Sorrow
tagline: A poet transforms grief into the most beautiful verse in Chinese history.

scenes.text: Song Dynasty China, 1127 CE. The Jurchen Jin have invaded and the emperor has fled south. Among the millions of refugees is China's greatest poet — Li Qingzhao — carrying a handcart of her most precious books and artwork.

scenes.speaker: Li Qingzhao
scenes.text: My husband gathered ten thousand books. We catalogued them by hand, argued over every character, drank wine in the lamplight. Now he is dead and the armies have taken even the books. What is left but words?

challenge.question: Li Qingzhao is regarded as:
options: The greatest female poet in Chinese literary history
The founder of the ci poetry form
challenge.fact: Li Qingzhao (1084–c.1155) is considered the greatest female poet in Chinese history and one of the greatest poets of all. She transformed the ci form — originally sung verses for entertainment — into a vehicle for profound personal expression.

scenes.text: Li Qingzhao broke the convention that ci poetry — song lyrics — was for lighthearted subjects. She poured grief, longing, and political despair into the form, permanently expanding what Chinese poetry could say.

challenge.instruction: Li Qingzhao's poems were set to music. Arrange this descending phrase — music of fading autumn.
challenge.fact: The ci poems of Li Qingzhao were written to specific tunes — each tune had a name and a set pattern of tones. Her poems about loss, love, and exile have been sung and recited for 900 years.

scenes.speaker: Li Qingzhao
scenes.text: I watch the chrysanthemums wilt on the windowsill. I used to write about their beauty with such ease. Now I understand that the poems worth writing are the ones that hurt to write.

challenge.question: Arrange these events of Li Qingzhao's life in chronological order:
items: Marries Zhao Mingcheng; together they collect bronzes, books, and paintings
Jin dynasty invades northern China; they flee south with what they can carry
Zhao Mingcheng dies; she loses most of her prized collection
Writes her most celebrated late poems — elegies of exile, loss, and autumn
challenge.fact: Li Qingzhao's life split sharply in two: the happy early years in Jinan collecting and writing beside her husband, and the desolate later years as a refugee. Her poem 'Sheng Sheng Man' opens with eighteen consecutive monosyllables evoking emptiness and longing — one of the most technically daring openings in all of Chinese poetry.

challenge.statement: After the death of her husband Zhao Mingcheng, Li Qingzhao continued to write — producing some of her most profound poems, marked by deep grief and longing.
challenge.fact: Li Qingzhao lost her husband, her home, and her famous art collection when the Jin dynasty invaded northern China in 1127. Her later ci poems are hauntingly different from her earlier joyful verses. She wrote: 'Who is left to share the fragrance of the wine?' — a line that still resonates 900 years later.

challenge.instruction: Arrange the opening of Genji's story as Murasaki Shikibu wrote it — the Emperor's doomed love for a lady not of the first rank.
challenge.fact: Written around 1008 CE by a court lady, The Tale of Genji is considered the world's first novel. Its author, known as Murasaki Shikibu, wrote in hiragana (considered 'women's script' then) while men wrote formal documents in Chinese — a subversion that produced one of humanity's great literary works.
